sub1: The supplied 24-line design with its two gate failures repaired and the rotation re-searched — every duty, every headcount and the whole coverage curve unchanged
coverNote: gaps of 6, 6, 6, 6 around the wheel — a perfect spread, kept through the search
h3: What was changed, and what could not be
sub3: One duty an hour shorter; everything else is the same work in a different order
h7: How it was repaired, and how to load it
sub7: Reproducible: the same starting grid, seed and objective give the same rotation on any machine
method:
1 · One duty, and it fixed both gates. The supplied grid was 60 minutes over the contracted week and carried one rest of 11h15 — line 7's Saturday 12:00–20:00 into line 8's Sunday 07:15–15:45. That turn is the only place 12:00–20:00 appears anywhere, and it sits in both failures. Shortening it to 12:00–19:00 removes exactly the 60 surplus minutes and lifts that rest to 12h15. Saturday cover at 19:00 goes from seven to six; nothing else moves.

2 · Then the shape was searched, not the staffing. Two moves only: swap two lines' duty within one day column, or swap two whole lines. Both leave each day's duties exactly as they were, so coverage, headcounts, the duty table and the contracted week are invariant by construction — the hour-by-hour heat map is identical to the supplied design's, and the search asserts that rather than assuming it. 60,000 candidates per restart, four restarts, four seeds, then a steepest-descent polish of every same-day swap and every pair of lines.

3 · The judge is the workspace's own — runDesignChecks, assessFatigue, assessHardLimits and scoreOrder, under anneal.mjs's measured weights. Four seeds gave four answers, all clearing every hard gate; this one is kept because it alone also clears FF15.
openQuestions: Both gates are clear and the staffing is untouched. 35h to the minute, no rest under 12h, longest run 6 — inside the design target of 7, not just the 13-day limit — and the cover weeks still perfectly even. One ORR factor remains present: FF19, a single start-time jump over two hours. FF15 is clear at 4. What could NOT be repaired by rearranging. The late-shorter-than-early lever is a property of the duty TABLE, not of the order: earlies and lates here both run 7h00–8h30, so no arrangement can make one strictly shorter than the other. Meeting it needs a different table, which is the trade By the Book makes and this design does not. Sunday's finish — five December movements fall after 23:25; this design inherits today's window rather than deciding it.

pickNote: How this one was picked: every row above clears all four hard gates and every one keeps the coverage curve identical — so the choice was between advisory outcomes, not safety. R21 is the only seed that also clears FF15, leaving a single factor present; R34 scores lower on the blended objective through a gentler 2h21 step, and R7 gives one more full weekend off. The blended score was NOT taken as the answer: fewer factors present is what the ORR panel reports and what a reader acts on. Wk fit is how evenly the weekday cover follows the December traffic curve, lower being more even.
